ESV.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.2: “Speak to all the congregation of the people of Israel and say to them, You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
ESV.3: Every one of you shall revere his mother and his father, and you shall keep my Sabbaths: I am the LORD your God.
ESV.4: Do not turn to idols or make for yourselves any gods of cast metal: I am the LORD your God.
ESV.5: “When you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.
ESV.6: It shall be eaten the same day you offer it or on the day after, and anything left over until the third day shall be burned up with fire.
ESV.7: If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is tainted; it will not be accepted,
ESV.8: and everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD, and that person shall be cut off from his people.
ESV.9: “When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap your field right up to its edge, neither shall you gather the gleanings after your harvest.
ESV.10: And you shall not strip your vineyard bare, neither shall you gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the sojourner: I am the LORD your God.
ESV.11: “You shall not steal; you shall not deal falsely; you shall not lie to one another.
ESV.12: You shall not swear by my name falsely, and so profane the name of your God: I am the LORD.
ESV.13: “You shall not oppress your neighbor or rob him. The wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you all night until the morning.
ESV.14: You shall not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God: I am the LORD.
ESV.15: “You shall do no injustice in court. You shall not be partial to the poor or defer to the great, but in righteousness shall you judge your neighbor.
ESV.16: You shall not go around as a slanderer among your people, and you shall not stand up against the life  of your neighbor: I am the LORD.
ESV.17: “You shall not hate your brother in your heart, but you shall reason frankly with your neighbor, lest you incur sin because of him.
ESV.18: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against the sons of your own people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
ESV.19: “You shall keep my statutes. You shall not let your cattle breed with a different kind. You shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed, nor shall you wear a garment of cloth made of two kinds of material.
ESV.20: “If a man lies sexually with a woman who is a slave, assigned to another man and not yet ransomed or given her freedom, a distinction shall be made. They shall not be put to death, because she was not free;
ESV.21: but he shall bring his compensation to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram for a guilt offering.
ESV.22: And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD for his sin that he has committed, and he shall be forgiven for the sin that he has committed.
ESV.23: “When you come into the land and plant any kind of tree for food, then you shall regard its fruit as forbidden.  Three years it shall be forbidden to you; it must not be eaten.
ESV.24: And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
ESV.25: But in the fifth year you may eat of its fruit, to increase its yield for you: I am the LORD your God.
ESV.26: “You shall not eat any flesh with the blood in it. You shall not interpret omens or tell fortunes.
ESV.27: You shall not round off the hair on your temples or mar the edges of your beard.
ESV.28: You shall not make any cuts on your body for the dead or tattoo yourselves: I am the LORD.
ESV.29: “Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land fall into prostitution and the land become full of depravity.
ESV.30: You shall keep my Sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary: I am the LORD.
ESV.31: “Do not turn to mediums or necromancers; do not seek them out, and so make yourselves unclean by them: I am the LORD your God.
ESV.32: “You shall stand up before the gray head and honor the face of an old man, and you shall fear your God: I am the LORD.
ESV.33: “When a stranger sojourns with you in your land, you shall not do him wrong.
ESV.34: You shall treat the stranger who sojourns with you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.
ESV.35: “You shall do no wrong in judgment, in measures of length or weight or quantity.
ESV.36: You shall have just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin:  I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
ESV.37: And you shall observe all my statutes and all my rules, and do them: I am the LORD.”

NASB.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NASB.2: 'Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel and say to them, 'You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
NASB.3: 'Every one of you shall reverence his mother and his father, and you shall keep My sabbaths; I am the LORD your God.
NASB.4: 'Do not turn to idols or make for yourselves molten gods; I am the LORD your God.
NASB.5: 'Now when you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.
NASB.6: 'It shall be eaten the same day you offer [it], and the next day; but what remains until the third day shall be burned with fire.
NASB.7: 'So if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an offense; it will not be accepted.
NASB.8: 'Everyone who eats it will bear his iniquity, for he has profaned the holy thing of the LORD; and that person shall be cut off from his people.
NASB.9: 'Now when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap to the very corners of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
NASB.10: 'Nor shall you glean your vineyard, nor shall you gather the fallen fruit of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the needy and for the stranger. I am the LORD your God.
NASB.11: 'You shall not steal, nor deal falsely, nor lie to one another.
NASB.12: 'You shall not swear falsely by My name, so as to profane the name of your God; I am the LORD.
NASB.13: 'You shall not oppress your neighbor, nor rob [him]. The wages of a hired man are not to remain with you all night until morning.
NASB.14: 'You shall not curse a deaf man, nor place a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall revere your God; I am the LORD.
NASB.15: 'You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not be partial to the poor nor defer to the great, but you are to judge your neighbor fairly.
NASB.16: 'You shall not go about as a slanderer among your people, and you are not to act against the life of your neighbor; I am the LORD.
NASB.17: 'You shall not hate your fellow countryman in your heart; you may surely reprove your neighbor, but shall not incur sin because of him.
NASB.18: 'You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the sons of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am the LORD.
NASB.19: 'You are to keep My statutes. You shall not breed together two kinds of your cattle; you shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed, nor wear a garment upon you of two kinds of material mixed together.
NASB.20: 'Now if a man lies carnally with a woman who is a slave acquired for [another] man, but who has in no way been redeemed nor given her freedom, there shall be punishment; they shall not, [however], be put to death, because she was not free.
NASB.21: 'He shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD to the doorway of the tent of meeting, a ram for a guilt offering.
NASB.22: 'The priest shall also make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD for his sin which he has committed, and the sin which he has committed will be forgiven him.
NASB.23: 'When you enter the land and plant all kinds of trees for food, then you shall count their fruit as forbidden. Three years it shall be forbidden to you; [it] shall not be eaten.
NASB.24: 'But in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
NASB.25: 'In the fifth year you are to eat of its fruit, that its yield may increase for you; I am the LORD your God.
NASB.26: 'You shall not eat [anything] with the blood, nor practice divination or soothsaying.
NASB.27: 'You shall not round off the side-growth of your heads nor harm the edges of your beard.
NASB.28: 'You shall not make any cuts in your body for the dead nor make any tattoo marks on yourselves: I am the LORD.
NASB.29: 'Do not profane your daughter by making her a harlot, so that the land will not fall to harlotry and the land become full of lewdness.
NASB.30: 'You shall keep My sabbaths and revere My sanctuary; I am the LORD.
NASB.31: 'Do not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out to be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
NASB.32: 'You shall rise up before the grayheaded and honor the aged, and you shall revere your God; I am the LORD.
NASB.33: 'When a stranger resides with you in your land, you shall not do him wrong.
NASB.34: 'The stranger who resides with you shall be to you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt; I am the LORD your God.
NASB.35: 'You shall do no wrong in judgment, in measurement of weight, or capacity.
NASB.36: 'You shall have just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin; I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.
NASB.37: 'You shall thus observe all My statutes and all My ordinances and do them; I am the LORD.''

NKJV.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NKJV.2: “Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
NKJV.3: ‘Every one of you shall revere his mother and his father, and keep My Sabbaths: I am the LORD your God.
NKJV.4: ‘Do not turn to idols, nor make for yourselves molded gods: I am the LORD your God.
NKJV.5: ‘And if you offer a sacrifice of a peace offering to the LORD, you shall offer it of your own free will.
NKJV.6: It shall be eaten the same day you offer it, and on the next day. And if any remains until the third day, it shall be burned in the fire.
NKJV.7: And if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination. It shall not be accepted.
NKJV.8: Therefore everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the hallowed offering of the LORD; and that person shall be cut off from his people.
NKJV.9: ‘When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
NKJV.10: And you shall not glean your vineyard, nor shall you gather every grape of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the stranger: I am the LORD your God.
NKJV.11: ‘You shall not steal, nor deal falsely, nor lie to one another.
NKJV.12: And you shall not swear by My name falsely, nor shall you profane the name of your God: I am the LORD.
NKJV.13: ‘You shall not cheat your neighbor, nor rob him. The wages of him who is hired shall not remain with you all night until morning.
NKJV.14: You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind, but shall fear your God: I am the LORD.
NKJV.15: ‘You shall do no injustice in judgment. You shall not be partial to the poor, nor honor the person of the mighty. In righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.
NKJV.16: You shall not go about as a talebearer among your people; nor shall you take a stand against the life of your neighbor: I am the LORD.
NKJV.17: ‘You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
NKJV.18: You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
NKJV.19: ‘You shall keep My statutes. You shall not let your livestock breed with another kind. You shall not sow your field with mixed seed. Nor shall a garment of mixed linen and wool come upon you.
NKJV.20: ‘Whoever lies carnally with a woman who is betrothed to a man as a concubine, and who has not at all been redeemed nor given her freedom, for this there shall be scourging; but they shall not be put to death, because she was not free.
NKJV.21: And he shall bring his trespass offering to the LORD, to the door of the tabernacle of meeting, a ram as a trespass offering.
NKJV.22: The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering before the LORD for his sin which he has committed. And the sin which he has committed shall be forgiven him.
NKJV.23: ‘When you come into the land, and have planted all kinds of trees for food, then you shall count their fruit as uncircumcised. Three years it shall be as uncircumcised to you. It shall not be eaten.
NKJV.24: But in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a praise to the LORD.
NKJV.25: And in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, that it may yield to you its increase: I am the LORD your God.
NKJV.26: ‘You shall not eat anything with the blood, nor shall you practice divination or soothsaying.
NKJV.27: You shall not shave around the sides of your head, nor shall you disfigure the edges of your beard.
NKJV.28: You shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor tattoo any marks on you: I am the LORD.
NKJV.29: ‘Do not prostitute your daughter, to cause her to be a harlot, lest the land fall into harlotry, and the land become full of wickedness.
NKJV.30: ‘You shall keep My Sabbaths and reverence My sanctuary: I am the LORD.
NKJV.31: ‘Give no regard to mediums and familiar spirits; do not seek after them, to be defiled by them: I am the LORD your God.
NKJV.32: ‘You shall rise before the gray headed and honor the presence of an old man, and fear your God: I am the LORD.
NKJV.33: ‘And if a stranger dwells with you in your land, you shall not mistreat him.
NKJV.34: The stranger who dwells among you shall be to you as one born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.
NKJV.35: ‘You shall do no injustice in judgment, in measurement of length, weight, or volume.
NKJV.36: You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
NKJV.37: ‘Therefore you shall observe all My statutes and all My judgments, and perform them: I am the LORD.’ ”

CSB17.9: “When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap to the very edge of your field or gather the gleanings <sup>ⓑ</sup> of your harvest.
CSB17.10: Do not strip your vineyard bare or gather its fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor <sup>ⓒ</sup> and the resident alien; <sup>ⓓ</sup> I am the LORD your God.
CSB17.11: “Do not steal. <sup>ⓔ</sup> Do not act deceptively <sup>ⓕ</sup> or lie <sup>ⓖ</sup> to one another.

CSB17.13: “Do not oppress <sup>ⓘ</sup> your neighbor or rob <sup>ⓙ</sup> him. The wages due a hired worker <sup>ⓚ</sup> must not remain with you until morning.
CSB17.14: Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block in front of the blind, <sup>ⓛ</sup> but you are to fear your God; <sup>ⓜ</sup> I am the LORD. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.15: “Do not act unjustly <sup>ⓐ</sup> when deciding a case. Do not be partial <sup>ⓑ</sup> to the poor or give preference to the rich; <sup>ⓒ</sup> judge your neighbor fairly.
CSB17.16: Do not go about spreading slander <sup>ⓓ</sup> among your people; do not jeopardize <sup>[1]</sup> your neighbor’s life; I am the LORD.
CSB17.17: “Do not harbor hatred against your brother. <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓔ</sup> Rebuke your neighbor directly, and you will not incur guilt because of him. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.18: Do not take revenge <sup>ⓖ</sup> or bear a grudge against members of your community, but love your neighbor as yourself; <sup>ⓗ</sup> I am the LORD.
CSB17.19: “You are to keep my statutes. Do not crossbreed two different kinds of your livestock, sow your fields with two kinds of seed, or put on a garment made of two kinds of material. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.20: “If a man has sexual intercourse with a woman who is a slave designated for another man, but she has not been redeemed <sup>ⓙ</sup> or given her freedom, there must be punishment. <sup>[3]</sup> They are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed.
CSB17.21: However, he must bring a ram as his guilt <sup>[4]</sup> offering to the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting. <sup>ⓚ</sup>

CSB17.23: “When you come into the land and plant any kind of tree for food, you are to consider the fruit forbidden. <sup>[5]</sup> It will be forbidden to you for three years; it is not to be eaten.
CSB17.24: In the fourth year all its fruit is to be consecrated as a praise offering <sup>ⓛ</sup> to the LORD.
CSB17.25: But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit. In this way its yield will increase for you; <sup>ⓜ</sup> I am the LORD your God.
CSB17.26: “You are not to eat anything with blood in it. <sup>[6]</sup> <sup>ⓝ</sup> You are not to practice divination <sup>ⓐ</sup> or witchcraft. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.27: You are not to cut off the hair at the sides of your head or mar the edge of your beard. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.28: You are not to make gashes on your bodies for the dead <sup>ⓓ</sup> or put tattoo marks on yourselves; I am the LORD.
CSB17.29: “Do not debase <sup>[7]</sup> <sup>ⓔ</sup> your daughter by making her a prostitute, <sup>ⓕ</sup> or the land will be prostituted and filled with depravity.
CSB17.30: Keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary; <sup>ⓖ</sup> I am the LORD.
CSB17.31: “Do not turn to mediums <sup>[8]</sup> <sup>ⓗ</sup> or consult spiritists, <sup>[9]</sup> <sup>ⓘ</sup> or you will be defiled by them; I am the LORD your God.
CSB17.32: “You are to rise in the presence of the elderly and honor the old. <sup>ⓙ</sup> Fear your God; I am the LORD.
CSB17.33: “When an alien resides with you in your land, you must not oppress <sup>ⓚ</sup> him.
CSB17.34: You will regard the alien who resides with you as the native-born among you. You are to love him as yourself, <sup>ⓛ</sup> for you were aliens in the land of Egypt; <sup>ⓜ</sup> I am the LORD your God.

NLT.1: The LORD also said to Moses,
NLT.2: “Give the following instructions to the entire community of Israel. You must be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
NLT.3: “Each of you must show great respect for your mother and father, and you must always observe my Sabbath days of rest. I am the LORD your God.
NLT.4: “Do not put your trust in idols or make metal images of gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
NLT.5: “When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, offer it properly so you will be accepted by God.
NLT.6: The sacrifice must be eaten on the same day you offer it or on the next day. Whatever is left over until the third day must be completely burned up.
NLT.7: If any of the sacrifice is eaten on the third day, it will be contaminated, and I will not accept it.
NLT.8: Anyone who eats it on the third day will be punished for defiling what is holy to the LORD and will be cut off from the community.
NLT.9: “When you harvest the crops of your land, do not harvest the grain along the edges of your fields, and do not pick up what the harvesters drop.
NLT.10: It is the same with your grape crop — do not strip every last bunch of grapes from the vines, and do not pick up the grapes that fall to the ground. Leave them for the poor and the foreigners living among you. I am the LORD your God.
NLT.11: “Do not steal. “Do not deceive or cheat one another.
NLT.12: “Do not bring shame on the name of your God by using it to swear falsely. I am the LORD.
NLT.13: “Do not defraud or rob your neighbor. “Do not make your hired workers wait until the next day to receive their pay.
NLT.14: “Do not insult the deaf or cause the blind to stumble. You must fear your God; I am the LORD.
NLT.15: “Do not twist justice in legal matters by favoring the poor or being partial to the rich and powerful. Always judge people fairly.
NLT.16: “Do not spread slanderous gossip among your people. “Do not stand idly by when your neighbor’s life is threatened. I am the LORD.
NLT.17: “Do not nurse hatred in your heart for any of your relatives. Confront people directly so you will not be held guilty for their sin.
NLT.18: “Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against a fellow Israelite, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
NLT.19: “You must obey all my decrees. “Do not mate two different kinds of animals. Do not plant your field with two different kinds of seed. Do not wear clothing woven from two different kinds of thread.
NLT.20: “If a man has sex with a slave girl whose freedom has never been purchased but who is committed to become another man’s wife, he must pay full compensation to her master. But since she is not a free woman, neither the man nor the woman will be put to death.
NLT.21: The man, however, must bring a ram as a guilt offering and present it to the LORD at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
NLT.22: The priest will then purify him before the LORD with the ram of the guilt offering, and the man’s sin will be forgiven.
NLT.23: “When you enter the land and plant fruit trees, leave the fruit unharvested for the first three years and consider it forbidden. Do not eat it.
NLT.24: In the fourth year the entire crop must be consecrated to the LORD as a celebration of praise.
NLT.25: Finally, in the fifth year you may eat the fruit. If you follow this pattern, your harvest will increase. I am the LORD your God.
NLT.26: “Do not eat meat that has not been drained of its blood. “Do not practice fortune-telling or witchcraft.
NLT.27: “Do not trim off the hair on your temples or trim your beards.
NLT.28: “Do not cut your bodies for the dead, and do not mark your skin with tattoos. I am the LORD.
NLT.29: “Do not defile your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will be filled with prostitution and wickedness.
NLT.30: “Keep my Sabbath days of rest, and show reverence toward my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
NLT.31: “Do not defile yourselves by turning to mediums or to those who consult the spirits of the dead. I am the LORD your God.
NLT.32: “Stand up in the presence of the elderly, and show respect for the aged. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
NLT.33: “Do not take advantage of foreigners who live among you in your land.
NLT.34: Treat them like native-born Israelites, and love them as you love yourself. Remember that you were once foreigners living in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
NLT.35: “Do not use dishonest standards when measuring length, weight, or volume.
NLT.36: Your scales and weights must be accurate. Your containers for measuring dry materials or liquids must be accurate. I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
NLT.37: “You must be careful to keep all of my decrees and regulations by putting them into practice. I am the LORD.”

WEB.2: “Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘You shall be holy; for I, Yahweh your God, am holy.

AMP.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.2: "Say to all the congregation of the children of Israel, 'You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
AMP.3: Each of you shall respect his mother and his father, and you shall keep My Sabbaths; I am the LORD your God.
AMP.4: Do not turn to idols or make for yourselves molten gods (images cast in metal); I am the LORD your God.
AMP.5: 'Now when you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.
AMP.6: It shall be eaten the same day you offer it and on the day following; and if anything remains until the third day, it shall be burned in the fire.
AMP.7: But if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is repulsive; it will not be accepted [by God as an offering].
AMP.8: Everyone who eats it will bear [the responsibility for] his wickedness, for he has profaned a holy thing of the LORD; and that person shall be cut off from his people [excluding him from the atonement made for them].
AMP.9: 'Now when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap to the very corners of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings (grain left after reaping) of your harvest.
AMP.10: And you shall not glean your vineyard, nor shall you gather its fallen grapes; you shall leave them for the poor and for the stranger. I am the LORD your God.
AMP.11: 'You shall not steal, nor deal deceptively, nor lie to one another.
AMP.12: You shall not swear [an oath] falsely by My name, so as to profane the name of your God; I am the LORD.
AMP.13: 'You shall not oppress or exploit your neighbor, nor rob him. You shall not withhold the wages of a hired man overnight until morning.
AMP.14: You shall not curse a deaf man nor put a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God [with profound reverence]; I am the LORD.
AMP.15: 'You shall not do injustice in judgment; you shall not be partial to the poor nor show a preference for the great, but judge your neighbor fairly.
AMP.16: You shall not go around as a gossip among your people, and you are not to act against the life of your neighbor [with slander or false testimony]; I am the LORD.
AMP.17: 'You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you may most certainly rebuke your neighbor, but shall not incur sin because of him.
AMP.18: You shall not take revenge nor bear any grudge against the sons of your people, but you shall love your neighbor (acquaintance, associate, companion) as yourself; I am the LORD.
AMP.19: 'You are to keep My statutes. You shall not breed together two kinds of your cattle; you shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed, nor wear clothing of two kinds of material mixed together.
AMP.20: 'Now if a man has intimate relations with a woman who is a slave acquired for [marriage to] another man, but who has not been redeemed nor given her freedom, there shall be punishment [after an investigation]; they shall not be put to death, because she was not free;
AMP.21: but he shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD to the doorway of the Tent of Meeting, a ram as a guilt offering.
AMP.22: The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD for his sin which he has committed; and he shall be forgiven for his sin.
AMP.23: 'When you enter the land and plant all kinds of trees for food, then you shall consider their fruit forbidden. For three years the fruit shall be forbidden to you; it shall not be eaten.
AMP.24: In the fourth year all the fruit shall be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
AMP.25: In the fifth year you may eat the fruit [of the trees], this is so that their yield may increase for you; I am the LORD your God.
AMP.26: 'You shall not eat anything with the blood, nor practice divination [using omens or witchcraft] or soothsaying.
AMP.27: You shall not trim and round off the side-growth of [the hair on] your heads, nor mar the edges of your beard.
AMP.28: You shall not make any cuts on your body [in mourning] for the dead, nor make any tattoo marks on yourselves; I am the LORD.
AMP.29: 'Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, so that the land will not fall to prostitution and become full of wickedness.
AMP.30: You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
AMP.31: 'Do not turn to mediums [who pretend to consult the dead] or to spiritists [who have spirits of divination]; do not seek them out to be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
AMP.32: 'You shall rise before the gray-headed and honor the aged, and you shall fear your God [with profound reverence]; I am the LORD.
AMP.33: 'When a stranger resides with you in your land, you shall not oppress or mistreat him.
AMP.34: But the stranger who resides with you shall be to you like someone native-born among you; and you shall love him as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt; I am the LORD your God.
AMP.35: 'You shall do no wrong in judgment, in measurement of weight or quantity.
AMP.36: You shall have just and accurate balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
AMP.37: You shall observe and keep all My statutes and all My ordinances and do them. I am the LORD.'"

NIV.1:
Various Laws
The Lord said to Moses,
NIV.2: “Speak to the entire assembly of Israel and say to them: ‘Be holy because I, the Lord your God, am holy.
NIV.3: “‘Each of you must respect his mother and father, and you must observe my Sabbaths. I am the Lord your God.
NIV.4: “‘Do not turn to idols or make gods of cast metal for yourselves. I am the Lord your God.
NIV.5: “‘When you sacrifice a fellowship offering to the Lord, sacrifice it in such a way that it will be accepted on your behalf.
NIV.6: It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it or on the next day; anything left over until the third day must be burned up.
NIV.7: If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is impure and will not be accepted.
NIV.8: Whoever eats it will be held responsible because he has desecrated what is holy to the Lord; that person must be cut off from his people.
NIV.9: “‘When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.
NIV.10: Do not go over your vineyard a second time or pick up the grapes that have fallen. Leave them for the poor and the alien. I am the Lord your God.
NIV.11:
“‘Do not steal.
“‘Do not lie.
“‘Do not deceive one another.
NIV.12: “‘Do not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the Lord.
NIV.13:
“‘Do not defraud your neighbor or rob him.
“‘Do not hold back the wages of a hired man overnight.
NIV.14: “‘Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block in front of the blind, but fear your God. I am the Lord.
NIV.15: “‘Do not pervert justice; do not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the great, but judge your neighbor fairly.
NIV.16:
“‘Do not go about spreading slander among your people.
“‘Do not do anything that endangers your neighbor’s life. I am the Lord.
NIV.17: “‘Do not hate your brother in your heart. Rebuke your neighbor frankly so you will not share in his guilt.
NIV.18: “‘Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against one of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord.
NIV.19:
“‘Keep my decrees.
“‘Do not mate different kinds of animals.
“‘Do not plant your field with two kinds of seed.
“‘Do not wear clothing woven of two kinds of material.
NIV.20: “‘If a man sleeps with a woman who is a slave girl promised to another man but who has not been ransomed or given her freedom, there must be due punishment. Yet they are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed.
NIV.21: The man, however, must bring a ram to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for a guilt offering to the Lord.
NIV.22: With the ram of the guilt offering the priest is to make atonement for him before the Lord for the sin he has committed, and his sin will be forgiven.
NIV.23: “‘When you enter the land and plant any kind of fruit tree, regard its fruit as forbidden. For three years you are to consider it forbidden; it must not be eaten.
NIV.24: In the fourth year all its fruit will be holy, an offering of praise to the Lord.
NIV.25: But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit. In this way your harvest will be increased. I am the Lord your God.
NIV.26:
“‘Do not eat any meat with the blood still in it.
“‘Do not practice divination or sorcery.
NIV.27: “‘Do not cut the hair at the sides of your head or clip off the edges of your beard.
NIV.28: “‘Do not cut your bodies for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the Lord.
NIV.29: “‘Do not degrade your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with wickedness.
NIV.30: “‘Observe my Sabbaths and have reverence for my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
NIV.31: “‘Do not turn to mediums or seek out spiritists, for you will be defiled by them. I am the Lord your God.
NIV.32: “‘Rise in the presence of the aged, show respect for the elderly and revere your God. I am the Lord.
NIV.33: “‘When an alien lives with you in your land, do not mistreat him.
NIV.34: The alien living with you must be treated as one of your native-born. Love him as yourself, for you were aliens in Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
NIV.35: “‘Do not use dishonest standards when measuring length, weight or quantity.
NIV.36: Use honest scales and honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt.
NIV.37: “‘Keep all my decrees and all my laws and follow them. I am the Lord.’”

NET.2: “Speak to the whole congregation of the Israelites and tell them, ‘You must be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
NET.3: Each of you must respect his mother and his father, and you must keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
NET.4: Do not turn to idols, and you must not make for yourselves gods of cast metal. I am the LORD your God.
NET.5: “‘When you sacrifice a peace offering sacrifice to the LORD, you must sacrifice it so that it is accepted for you.
NET.6: It must be eaten on the day of your sacrifice and on the following day, but what is left over until the third day must be burned up.
NET.7: If, however, it is eaten on the third day, it is spoiled, it will not be accepted,
NET.8: and the one who eats it will bear his punishment for iniquity because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person will be cut off from his people.
NET.9: “‘When you gather in the harvest of your land, you must not completely harvest the corner of your field, and you must not gather up the gleanings of your harvest.
NET.10: You must not pick your vineyard bare, and you must not gather up the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You must leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
NET.11: “‘You must not steal, you must not tell lies, and you must not deal falsely with your fellow citizen.
NET.12: You must not swear falsely in my name, so that you do not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
NET.13: You must not oppress your neighbor or commit robbery against him. You must not withhold the wages of the hired laborer overnight until morning.
NET.14: You must not curse a deaf person or put a stumbling block in front of a blind person. You must fear your God; I am the LORD.
NET.15: “‘You must not deal unjustly in judgment: you must neither show partiality to the poor nor honor the rich. You must judge your fellow citizen fairly.
NET.16: You must not go about as a slanderer among your people. You must not stand idly by when your neighbor’s life is at stake. I am the LORD.
NET.17: You must not hate your brother in your heart. You must surely reprove your fellow citizen so that you do not incur sin on account of him.
NET.18: You must not take vengeance or bear a grudge against the children of your people, but you must love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
NET.19: You must keep my statutes. You must not allow two different kinds of your animals to breed, you must not sow your field with two different kinds of seed, and you must not wear a garment made of two different kinds of fabric.
NET.20: “‘When a man has sexual intercourse with a woman, although she is a slave woman designated for another man and she has not yet been ransomed, or freedom has not been granted to her, there will be an obligation to pay compensation. They must not be put to death, because she was not free.
NET.21: He must bring his guilt offering to the LORD at the entrance of the Meeting Tent, a guilt offering ram,
NET.22: and the priest is to make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD for his sin that he has committed, and he will be forgiven of his sin that he has committed.
NET.23: “‘When you enter the land and plant any fruit tree, you must consider its fruit to be forbidden. Three years it will be forbidden to you; it must not be eaten.
NET.24: In the fourth year all its fruit will be holy, praise offerings to the LORD.
NET.25: Then in the fifth year you may eat its fruit to add its produce to your harvest. I am the LORD your God.
NET.26: “‘You must not eat anything with the blood still in it. You must not practice either divination or soothsaying.
NET.27: You must not round off the corners of the hair on your head or ruin the corners of your beard.
NET.28: You must not slash your body for a dead person or incise a tattoo on yourself. I am the LORD.
NET.29: Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, so that the land does not practice prostitution and become full of lewdness.
NET.30: “‘You must keep my Sabbaths and fear my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
NET.31: Do not turn to the spirits of the dead and do not seek familiar spirits to become unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.
NET.32: You must stand up in the presence of the aged, honor the presence of an elder, and fear your God. I am the LORD.
NET.33: When a foreigner resides with you in your land, you must not oppress him.
NET.34: The foreigner who resides with you must be to you like a native citizen among you; so you must love him as yourself, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
NET.35: You must not do injustice in the regulation of measures, whether of length, weight, or volume.
NET.36: You must have honest balances, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt.
NET.37: You must be sure to obey all my statutes and regulations. I am the LORD.’”
